BRIEF REASONS FOR THE JUST DECISION OF THE CASE Digitally signed by FIR No. 535/2006 State Vs. Sarvan ISRA ISRA ZAIDI ZAIDI 2026.02.10 16:15:08 +0800 06.

In the instant case, in order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution had to prove the following ingredients of the offence punishable u/s 408 and u/s. 285/336/34 IPC and 7 E.C. IPC beyond reasonable doubt.

It is apt to quote the following sections :
Section 408 IPC:-
"Whoever, being a clerk or servant or employed as a clerk or servant, and being in any manner entrusted in such capacity with property, or with any dominion over property, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."
Section 285 IPC:-
"Whoever does, with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person,
or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both."

Section 336 IPC:-
"Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may FIR No. 535/2006 State Vs. Sarvan ISRA by ISRA ZAIDI ZAIDI 2026.02.10 16:15:14 +0800 extend to two hundred and fifty rupees, or with both."

Section 7 E.C:-
"If any person contravenes any order made under section 3,
--(a)he shall be punishable,--(i)in the case of an order made with reference to clause (h) or clause (i) of sub-section (2) of that section, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and shall also be liable to fine, and(ii)in the case of any State vs Sarwan on 10 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36678158/
4 other order, with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine:Provided that the court may, for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment,
impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term of less than three months;(b)any property in respect of which the order has been contravened shall be forfeited to the Government;(c)any package, covering or receptacle in which the property is found and any animal, vehicle, vessel or other conveyance used in carrying the commodity shall, if the court so orders, be forfeited to the Government."
07.
Needless to mention, in criminal law, the burden of proof on the prosecution is that of beyond reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by adducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.

35. The case of the prosecution also suffers from various infirmities regarding the alleged raid and recovery.

All recovery witnesses are police officials, and no independent public witness was joined at the time of seizure despite fact that the alleged spot was situated in a residential-cum-industrial area with several houses in close proximity.

particularly when the place of occurrence was not isolated, casts a serious doubt on the alleged recovery proceedings.

43. For the reasons outlined above, this court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to discharge the heavy burden imposed on it by law of satisfying this court beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the accused persons.
